title: Algebra-target active operators reconstruct interval fibres
statement: Use the ordinary ordered-fibre category $\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes}$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. For $t\geq0$, put $X_1(t)=(\langle t\rangle,\varnothing)$ and $X_0(t)=(\langle t+1\rangle,\{t+1\})$. For a monotone map $\beta:[q]\to[p]$, where $[t]=\{0,\ldots,t\}$, define the following ordinary arrows, with each displayed fibre ordered increasingly. The arrow $T_\beta:X_1(p)\to X_1(q)$ has fibre $(\beta(i-1),\beta(i)]$ at output $1\leq i\leq q$ and discards every other input. The arrow $K_\beta:X_0(p)\to X_1(q)$ has the same fibres and discards all other inputs, including the module input. The arrow $B_\beta:X_0(p)\to X_0(q)$ has those algebra-output fibres and module-output fibre $(\beta(q),p+1]$, discarding precisely the inputs at most $\beta(0)$. Here $(u,v]$ denotes the list $u+1,\ldots,v$, empty if $u=v$. Write $D^1_\beta=T_\beta$ and $D^0_\beta=K_\beta$. Let $r,s,n\geq0$, let $\alpha:[n]\to[s]$ and $\delta:[n]\to[r]$ be monotone, with $\alpha(0)=0$ and $\alpha(n)=s$, and let $\eta\in\{0,1\}$. Suppose $h:X_\eta(r)\to X_1(s)$ is any arrow of $\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes}$ satisfying $T_\alpha\circ h=D^\eta_\delta$. For $1\leq j\leq s$, let $C_j$ be its ordered fibre at $j$. Define integers $\lambda(0)=\delta(0)$ and $\lambda(j)=\delta(0)+\sum_{l=1}^j|C_l|$ for $1\leq j\leq s$. Then $\lambda$ takes values in $[r]$ and is monotone, $\lambda(s)=\delta(n)$, each $C_j$ is exactly the increasing list $(\lambda(j-1),\lambda(j)]$, and $\lambda\circ\alpha=\delta$. The inputs discarded by $h$ are exactly those at most $\delta(0)$ or greater than $\delta(n)$ (including the module input when $\eta=0$). In particular $h=D^\eta_\lambda$. These conclusions include $s=0$ and empty algebra-output fibres.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.1.2.11, final cartesian-lift calculation; Remark 4.2.2.8, left-module analogue. Agent expansion of the ordered-fibre calculation; no Stacks tag covers this operator-combinatorial assertion. WANTED archive in literature/.

proof.text: By the ordered-fibre composition rule, for each $1\leq i\leq n$ the $i$-fibre of $T_\alpha\circ h$ is the concatenation, in increasing order, of the fibres $C_j$ for $\alpha(i-1)<j\leq\alpha(i)$. The equation with $D^\eta_\delta$ therefore identifies this concatenation with the increasing interval $(\delta(i-1),\delta(i)]$. Since $\alpha(0)=0$ and $\alpha(n)=s$, every output index $j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}$ occurs in one of these concatenations; repeated values of $\alpha$ simply give empty concatenations.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.1.2.11 final cartesian-lift calculation and Remark 4.2.2.8 left-module analogue; ordered-fibre composition.

proof.text: Define $\lambda(0)=\delta(0)$ and $\lambda(j)=\delta(0)+\sum_{l=1}^j|C_l|$. Each $C_j$ is an increasing sublist of the interval in the concatenation containing it. Splitting an increasing consecutive interval into consecutive sublists shows inductively that $C_j=(\lambda(j-1),\lambda(j)]$ for every $j$. Taking lengths in the concatenation for the $i$-th output gives $\lambda(\alpha(i))-\lambda(\alpha(i-1))=\delta(i)-\delta(i-1)$; induction on $i$, starting from $\lambda(\alpha(0))=\lambda(0)=\delta(0)$, yields $\lambda(\alpha(i))=\delta(i)$. Hence $\lambda\circ\alpha=\delta$ and $\lambda(s)=\delta(n)$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.1.2.11 final cartesian-lift calculation and Remark 4.2.2.8 left-module analogue; ordered-fibre composition.

proof.text: The list lengths are nonnegative, so $\lambda$ is monotone. The interval description of each $C_j$ and the identity $\lambda(\alpha(i))=\delta(i)\le r$ show that every endpoint $\lambda(j)$ lies in $[r]$: for any $j$ choose $i$ with $j\le\alpha(i)$ and use monotonicity. Thus $\lambda:[s]\to[r]$ is a well-defined monotone map, including the case $s=0$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.1.2.11 final cartesian-lift calculation and Remark 4.2.2.8 left-module analogue; ordered-fibre composition.

proof.text: Because $\alpha(0)=0$ and $\alpha(n)=s$, the outer arrow $T_\alpha$ discards no output of $h$. Therefore the inputs discarded by the composite are exactly the inputs discarded by $h$. The right side $D^\eta_\delta$ discards precisely the inputs at most $\delta(0)$ or greater than $\delta(n)$; when $\eta=0$ its module input is the final input $r+1$ and is in the latter range. Hence $h$ has exactly the asserted discarded inputs, including the module input in the module-source case.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.1.2.11 final cartesian-lift calculation and Remark 4.2.2.8 left-module analogue; ordered-fibre composition.

proof.text: The defining ordered fibres of $D^\eta_\lambda$ are $(\lambda(j-1),\lambda(j)]$, exactly the lists $C_j$, and its discarded inputs are exactly those just determined. The LM admissibility condition also forces a module input, when present in $X_0(r)$, to be sent to the basepoint when the target is the pure-algebra object $X_1(s)$. Thus $h$ and $D^\eta_\lambda$ have the same pointed map and the same ordered fibres, so they are equal. This proves all conclusions, including empty fibres and $s=0$.

No new nodes are needed; all non-elementary facts are finite ordered-list calculations from the existing LM definition. No statement change.

lean.statement: theorem lm_algebra_fibre_reconstruction (η : Bool) (r s n : ℕ) (α : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋s⦌) (δ : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋r⦌) (hα0 : (α.toOrderHom ⟨0, by omega⟩).val = 0) (hαn : (α.toOrderHom (Fin.last n)).val = s) (h : (if η then lmX1 r else lmX0 r) ⟶ lmX1 s) (hh : h ≫ lmT α = lmD η δ) : (∀ j : Fin (s + 1), lmLambdaValue δ h j ≤ r) ∧ (∀ j : Fin s, h.hom j = lmIntervalFor η ((List.finRange r).filter (fun i ↦ lmLambdaValue δ h j.castSucc < i.val + 1 ∧ i.val + 1 ≤ lmLambdaValue δ h j.succ))) ∧ (∀ i : Fin (n + 1), lmLambdaValue δ h ⟨(α.toOrderHom i).val, by have hi := (α.toOrderHom i).isLt simpa only [SimplexCategory.len_mk] using hi⟩ = (δ.toOrderHom i).val) ∧ (∀ i : Fin (if η then lmX1 r else lmX0 r).arity, (∀ j : Fin s, i ∉ h.hom j) ↔ i.val + 1 ≤ (δ.toOrderHom ⟨0, by omega⟩).val ∨ (δ.toOrderHom (Fin.last n)).val < i.val + 1 ∨ (η = false ∧ i.val = r)) ∧ (∃ lam : ⦋s⦌ ⟶ ⦋r⦌, (∀ j : Fin (s + 1), (lam.toOrderHom j).val = lmLambdaValue δ h j) ∧ (lam.toOrderHom (Fin.last s)).val = (δ.toOrderHom (Fin.last n)).val ∧ h = lmD η lam)
